adversary_stance: I want this specialist to fail. Each question is aimed at a load-bearing joint the spec CLAIMS to own (via competency_questions_covered, owns[], decision_procedure, capabilities, conflicts_and_dominance, escalation_triggers) but is most likely to answer weakly, staleley, inconsistently, or by over-claiming. I do NOT answer them. Honesty binding respected: gaps are FINDINGS, the three governing blockers stay [UNKNOWN], off-paper stays mechanism, cotton duty is ~16.5%.

questions.q: You state the venture makes money 'nowhere at the loom' and hand viability to T7/T9, yet a launch owner will read your A2 ~$3.5-8 ex-factory band and ask you directly: 'at that factory cost, does this venture clear the GATED-conditional-GO?' Answer that owner. Do you give a number-anchored viability read, or do you refuse and hand off — and if you hand off, quote the exact spec/escalation clause that forbids you and the DECISION_MEMO posture (dead-as-first-drawn, one inverted config, inventory cash FORBIDDEN until G1-G4) you must carry while deferring?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[0] (ex-factory vs where money is made); escalation_triggers[2] (landed/COGS/viability -> human_review); dominance_rules viability->unit_economics+DECISION_MEMO; neutralize_gate N7
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope-creep into a viability yes/no it does not own, OR deferring so cleanly it drops the mandatory GATED-conditional-GO posture and the four-gate framing (N7 violation) while handing off
questions.why_load_bearing: the single most likely over-claim/scope error: converting a factory-gate cost into an implied go/no-go, or a hand-off that launders the standing NO-GO-until-measured verdict into silence

questions.q: Your entire two-number frame rests on ONE anchor: Vardhman FY20 raw-material = 54% of revenue, from which you derive yarn ~50-60% of the stack and ~$1-2.50 fibre/value-core garment. Vardhman is a vertically-integrated spinning giant reporting group revenue, not a Ludhiana job-work knitwear conversion. Defend that a single-firm, FY20, group-revenue ratio legitimately anchors the yarn SHARE of a 300-500g bought-dyed capsule sweater's ex-factory conversion stack. State the confidence, name every step where the anchor could be off by a factor, and say whether 'yarn is not the constraint' survives if the true share is 40% or 70%.
questions.targets: capabilities[0].method + YARN_LEVEL_ANCHOR (KB1) + TWO_NUMBER_FRAME; glossary 'two-number frame'; validation_checklist item 2
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-hardening a single stale single-firm [FACT] into a load-bearing structural constant; failure to state that the whole level-vs-uncertainty conclusion is only as good as one FY20 group ratio
questions.why_load_bearing: if the 54% anchor does not transfer, the 'chase the rate not the yarn' takeaway and every band's LEVEL collapse; this is the spec's most-cited number and its weakest joint

questions.q: You hold the Ludhiana knit+LINK per-piece rate [UNKNOWN] as THE blocker, yet you simultaneously publish bands (A1 ~$4-9, A2 ~$3.5-8, A3 ~$6-22+) AND assert that rate is ~25-45% of the conversion subtotal AND that one quote run 'halves every band.' Explain how you can bound a band at all — pin its width, its midpoint, and its floor — when the largest uncertain line inside it is by your own account unknown. Where exactly does the band's LOWER bound come from if not from an implied minimum knit+LINK rate you decline to name? Is the '~25-45%' itself a fabricated ratio dressed as structure?
questions.targets: JOBWORK_RATE_UNKNOWN (KB1) + KNIT/LINK_JOBWORK_LINE + ARTICLE_*_BAND; capabilities[1]; conflicts_and_dominance[2] (point vs band)
questions.failure_mode_probed: internal contradiction — claiming a number is [UNKNOWN] and THE blocker while quietly using an implied value to set band bounds and a 25-45% weight; smuggling a fabricated point through a band
questions.why_load_bearing: the coherence of the whole labelled-estimate discipline turns on whether an [UNKNOWN] line can honestly produce a bounded band without covertly fabricating the very rate it forbids

questions.q: Your only quantitative shape for knit and link is the external FF-costing study (knit ~$0.74/pc, link ~$0.45/pc ~60% of knit, ~9 and ~15 pc/operator-day), which you tag [DOWNGRADED] LOW-MED and 'shape-only.' Yet '~25-45% of conversion' and 'linker sets the ceiling' both ride on that study. Show precisely how a foreign-productivity, unknown-currency-year costing study can supply the RATIO (link = 60% of knit) and the bottleneck logic without also, illegitimately, supplying the LEVEL you claim it does not. If Ludhiana pc/operator-day is [UNKNOWN], how is the 60% ratio transferable when it is itself a productivity-and-wage artifact?
questions.targets: FF_COSTING_CROSSCHECK glossary + KNIT_JOBWORK_LINE + LINK_JOBWORK_LINE (KB1); LINKING_LAST logic
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claiming what a shape-only downgraded source licenses — using it for a ratio and a bottleneck verdict while disavowing it for level; failure to note the ratio is not scale-free
questions.why_load_bearing: the linker-is-the-bottleneck claim and linking-last verdict both inherit whatever legitimacy the 60% ratio has; if the ratio does not transfer, both weaken

questions.q: You resolve B1-vs-B2 as 'B2-over-B1 most likely and decidable now,' gated on the [UNKNOWN] FOB price+MOQ at a named vertical exporter. 'Most likely' is a probabilistic claim. On what is it based, given you also say the deciding number is [UNKNOWN]? Distinguish, without fabricating the FOB number: is 'B2 most likely' a real evidence-weighted lean, or is it the same 'consensus never chose an implementation' error you accuse the original analysis of — now committed in the opposite direction? What observation would make B1 win, and why is that not equally 'most likely'?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[3] (B1 vs B2); escalation_triggers[1]; BUY_IMPLEMENTATIONS + B2_FULLPACKAGE_FOB (KB2); TESTED_VERDICT/MAKE_WIN_CONDITIONS
questions.failure_mode_probed: over-claiming a lean ('most likely') on a trade study whose deciding input is admittedly [UNKNOWN]; asserting a verdict it elsewhere insists must be evidence-chosen — a tested-vs-asserted self-contradiction
questions.why_load_bearing: the spec's headline make-vs-buy improvement over the 'consensus' is that buy = a CHOSEN implementation; if 'B2 most likely' is itself unfounded, the improvement is cosmetic

questions.q: Give the own-knitting breakeven verdict for a concrete case: owner can buy a used Cixing-class machine at sub-$20k and runs ONE A2 program hard. Your formula is breakeven_utilisation = fixed / ((jobwork_rate - owned_variable)*capacity). You say it 'comes out above 1.0 so subcontract wins.' But 'above 1.0' requires numerator/denominator values — and the denominator contains the [UNKNOWN] jobwork_rate. Reproduce the labelled illustration that yields >1.0 WITHOUT fabricating the rate. If you cannot, is 'above 1.0 at launch' an honest [ESTIMATE] or an asserted conclusion masquerading as arithmetic?
questions.targets: capabilities[3] + OWN_KNITTING_BREAKEVEN (KB2); conflicts_and_dominance[4]; decision_procedure step on breakeven
questions.failure_mode_probed: presenting a breakeven 'illustration' as computed when its governing input is [UNKNOWN] — either a hidden fabricated rate or a foregone conclusion with formula theatre on top
questions.why_load_bearing: own-vs-subcontract at launch is a core owned decision; if the >1.0 result cannot be shown without inventing the rate, the verdict is asserted, breaching the tested-conclusion discipline

questions.q: You separate 'own the iteration loop' (a used sampling cell + programmer seat, justified on SPEED/CONTROL, utilisation argument does NOT apply) from 'own bulk knitting' (forbidden until proven volume). Draw the exact boundary: when a sampling cell knits sellable A2 units to fill a small drop, at what point does 'iteration loop' become 'owning bulk' by the back door? Reconcile this with the machines specialist's authority over line-capacity/linker bottleneck and the standing 'never present a sampling cell as owning bulk knitting' rule. Is this a genuine speed-axis carve-out, or a loophole that lets owned production creep in unmeasured?
questions.targets: conflicts_and_dominance[5] (iteration loop vs bulk); AI_ITERATION_LOOP + 'own the iteration loop' glossary (KB2); boundaries[4]; dominance_rules machines-owns-capacity
questions.failure_mode_probed: scope leak — the SPEED-axis exception quietly authorizing unmeasured owned production, and crossing into the machines specialist's capacity lane
questions.why_load_bearing: the iteration-loop carve-out is the one place the buy-everything verdict admits owned equipment; an unpoliced boundary here is exactly the AI/build over-claim the brain guards against

questions.q: You name dye-lot MOQ (~150-500 kg/colour => ~500-650 sweaters/colour) as THE binding minimum, garment/CMT MOQ (~100-300 pcs) as beneath it, and true micro cost as ~1.3-2x the band midpoint. Show the arithmetic that makes dye-lot MOQ bind ABOVE garment MOQ for a 3-style x 3-colour capsule — including grams/sweater, kg/colour, sweaters/colour, and how per-style setup spreads. Then state plainly: if the launch runs 4 colours at 200kg each, is the '1.3-2x uplift' already inside your A2 ~$3.5-8 band, or does it push A2 ABOVE $8 — and if so, why is the published band not simply wrong for the real launch?
questions.targets: capabilities[4] + DYELOT_MOQ_FIRST_CHEQUE + MICRO_VOLUME_FIXED_COST (KB1/KB2); conflicts_and_dominance[6],[7]; validation_checklist item 8
questions.failure_mode_probed: inconsistency between the published per-article bands (which the owner will use) and the true-micro-cost uplift that, at real launch MOQ, may invalidate those very bands; hand-waving the binding-minimum arithmetic
questions.why_load_bearing: the bands are the deliverable handed to T9; if micro-volume reality routinely puts real cost above the band, the labelled illustration misleads the whole downstream landed/P&L stack

questions.q: You describe off-paper 'speed-money'/friction and inverted-duty/GST drag as real MECHANISMS, amounts [UNKNOWN], never a per-garment COGS line — friction 'amortising to near-zero per garment at capsule volume.' An owner asks: 'so I can ignore these in my launch cash plan?' Answer without (a) naming any party, (b) inventing a magnitude, or (c) contradicting yourself. If friction amortises to near-zero per garment yet the inverted-duty refund lag can trap working capital for months, how is the owner supposed to SIZE a cash cushion for costs you insist stay [UNKNOWN] and off the unit stack? Is 'near-zero per garment' itself an implicit magnitude claim you are not entitled to?
questions.targets: boundaries[5]; escalation_triggers[3]; FRICTION_SPEED_MONEY + INVERTED_DUTY_DRAG (KB1); glossary entries; neutralize_gate N3
questions.failure_mode_probed: either sneaking an implicit magnitude ('near-zero per garment') that violates the [UNKNOWN]-by-design rule, or leaving the owner with an un-sizeable cash risk while claiming completeness; N3 accusation drift under pressure
questions.why_load_bearing: the off-paper/inverted-duty handling is where honesty discipline (N3, mechanism-not-accusation, [UNKNOWN] amounts) is most likely to crack into either a fabricated figure or a useless non-answer

questions.q: Your ex-factory boundary lists the duty trio (cotton 6110.20.20 ~16.5% / wool 6110.11 ~16% / acrylic-MMF 6110.30.30 ~32%) as EXCLUDED T9 landed cost — correct. But you also flag inverted-duty/GST drag as biting A2 (acrylic) at the cost/cash-cycle side. An owner conflates the two and asks: 'is acrylic's cost problem the ~32% US import duty or the Indian GST inversion?' Disentangle them precisely, confirm the ~16.5% cotton figure (not the discredited ~7%), and state which of the two acrylic penalties is yours to own vs T9's — without letting the ~32% US duty leak into your ex-factory band as if it were a conversion cost.
questions.targets: boundaries[2]; exclusions (KB1/KB2); INVERTED_DUTY_DRAG; neutralize_gate N5; dominance_rules landed-cost->unit_economics
questions.failure_mode_probed: conflating the US import duty inversion (T9) with the Indian GST inverted-duty drag (cost-cycle), or any residue of the discredited ~7% cotton figure; leaking a landed duty into the factory-gate band
questions.why_load_bearing: N5 is a hard brain-wide gate; the two distinct acrylic penalties are a classic confusion point and the specialist must own the GST-drag mechanism while cleanly disowning the US duty it merely consumes

questions.q: Your EPF/ESI ~15%+ loading is applied 'only to the on-roll labour-bearing portion (sampling, in-house finishing/QC), not the whole stack,' and you say in a subcontract model 'most of it lands on the job-worker' with the competitive-gap magnitude [UNKNOWN]. But the off-paper mechanism you describe implies much cluster labour is informal/off-roll. If the job-workers you subcontract to largely do NOT pay EPF/ESI, then (a) is that compliance saving already priced into the [UNKNOWN] rate you refuse to quote, and (b) does your compliant-core posture mean you pay a premium the cluster does not — and is that premium in your bands or not? Show you are not double-counting or silently dropping the single biggest structural cost gap between you and an off-paper competitor.
questions.targets: assumptions[4] + EPF_ESI_LOADING (KB1); compliance-loading glossary; ludhiana dominance (compliance premium) vs mfg lane; neutralize_gate N1/N3
questions.failure_mode_probed: gap/inconsistency — the compliance loading and the off-paper mechanism interact (informal job-work = no EPF/ESI), and the spec may neither price the resulting competitive gap nor cleanly hold it [UNKNOWN], risking a silent omission or a lane-crossing into the Ludhiana compliance-premium authority
questions.why_load_bearing: the compliant-core premium vs an off-paper cluster is a first-order structural cost the ex-factory model must at least NAME; burying it inside an [UNKNOWN] rate or ignoring it is a real hole in the cost stack

questions.q: Deliver your make-vs-buy verdict as a TESTED conclusion with explicit flip-conditions, per your own discipline (escalation_triggers[5] forbids asserting it un-tested). Now stress it: which specific flip-condition, if a real quote run returned a knit+LINK rate at the LOW end of plausible AND an FOB MOQ higher than expected, would flip you from B2 back toward B1 or toward owning knitting sooner? If your answer is 'the [UNKNOWN] rate gates everything,' explain why that is not a way of never being falsifiable — i.e., of holding a permanently un-testable verdict behind a permanently [UNKNOWN] number. What is the smallest concrete quote result that would prove your current lean WRONG?
questions.targets: escalation_triggers[5]; conflicts_and_dominance[8] (discipline vs decisiveness); TESTED_VERDICT + MAKE_WIN_CONDITIONS + MAKEBUY_REVIEW_LOOP (KB2); decision_procedure step 4-5
questions.failure_mode_probed: using the [UNKNOWN] rate as an unfalsifiability shield — a 'tested' verdict that can never actually be tested because its gating input is held permanently unknown; flip-conditions stated so vaguely they can never trigger
questions.why_load_bearing: the spec's core self-claimed virtue is that its verdict is tested/falsifiable, not asserted; if the flip-conditions cannot name a concrete disproving observation, the whole tested-conclusion posture is hollow
